extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), school administrators, HR and legal counsel implementing Title IX
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory preamble to the final Title IX regulations describing recipients' obligations and regulatory standards concerning pregnancy, related conditions, voluntary leave, lactation time and space, comparable treatment to temporary medical conditions, and related pre-employment inquiries and scope of sex discrimination coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on employment discrimination for pregnancy or related conditions (§106.57(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not discriminate against employees on the basis of current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions. The Department changed the word 'shall' to 'must' and removed the words 'or exclude from employment' from §106.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets 'discriminate' to encompass exclusion. This provision is intended to update and comprehensively protect employees from pregnancy-related barriers to professional achievement and career opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for students (framework) (§106.40(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide students reasonable modifications based on pregnancy or related conditions as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework is individualized and flexible, requiring consultation with the student and allowing responses to a wide variety of circumstances and employment contexts when a student's on-campus employment is part of or necessary to access their education. The Department declined to require identical reasonable modification protections for employees at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable treatment for employees to other temporary medical conditions (§106.57(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions as any other temporary medical condition for all job-related purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated job-related purposes include commencement, duration and extensions of leave, payment of disability income, accrual of seniority, reinstatement, and any other benefit or service and any fringe benefit offered to employees by virtue of employment. The final text replaces references to 'temporary disability' with 'temporary medical conditions' and removes 'or any temporary disability resulting therefrom' to avoid implying pregnancy itself is a disability. If an employee's pregnancy-related condition qualifies as a disability, ADA/Section 504 may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary leaves of absence for pregnancy or related conditions (§106.57(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not maintain a leave policy, or an employee lacks sufficient accrued leave to qualify under the recipient's policy, the recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions as a justification for an employee's voluntary leave of absence for a reasonable period of time and must reinstate the employee after such time to the status held when the leave began or to a comparable position without negative effect on rights or privileges of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'voluntary' clarifies that an employee must not be forced to take leave due to pregnancy. 'Reasonable period of time' is a fact-specific inquiry considering the totality of circumstances, including the period deemed medically necessary by the employee's health care provider. If a recipient's leave policy is more generous, the recipient must permit the employee to take leave under that policy instead. The Department declined to adopt a blanket right to all medically necessary time off for employees at this time due to interplay with recent Federal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation time and space access for employees (§106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure that an employee can access a lactation space (other than a bathroom) that is clean, private, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used by an employee for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding as needed, and must provide reasonable break time to express breast milk or breastfeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department changed the phrasing from 'ensure the availability of a lactation space' to 'ensure that an employee can access a lactation space' to emphasize accessibility. Whether a space meets the standards is case-by-case but generally means functional, appropriate, and safe for use. No additional specific size, equipment, or number-of-spaces requirements were mandated to preserve recipient flexibility. Recipients must also comply with applicable Federal, State, or local lactation laws that may impose more specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility within reasonable break time (lactation) (§106.57(e)(2) implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lactation space must be accessible to the employee within the reasonable break time provided so that the employee can get there and back, express milk or breastfeed, and store expressed milk within the allotted time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the lactation space is so far from an employee's workstation that the employee cannot reasonably use it within break time, the Department would not consider the space accessible. This parallels student lactation access requirements under §106.40(b)(3)(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared lactation space solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple students or employees need simultaneous access to a lactation space, a recipient must develop a solution consistent with §106.57(e)(2) that meets users' needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable solutions may include signage, a scheduling system, partitions or screens to allow simultaneous use, or other arrangements tailored to the institution. The Department declined to mandate a particular arrangement but requires that obligations under §106.57(e)(2) be met for each user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breastfeeding vs. pumping and presence of infants
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may use the designated lactation space for breastfeeding instead of pumping if the employee has access to their child while at work; the provision does not require recipients to allow nursing infants in other workplace areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a child may be present in recipient spaces outside the lactation room is fact-specific and may be governed by State/local laws. Employees may also choose to express milk or breastfeed outside the designated lactation spaces if State and local laws allow it. §106.57(e) requires access regardless of the employee's gender identity or whether they plan to pump or breastfeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical documentation for lactation needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes it is not reasonable to require medical documentation for lactation needs because initiation of lactation after childbirth is nearly universal; for students the Department added §106.40(b)(3)(vi) prohibiting requiring supporting documentation for lactation-related modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For employees, the Department declined at this time to adopt a similar prohibition and will consider interplay with other Federal laws (e.g., PUMP Act, PWFA). The Department reminds recipients that documentation for pregnancy or related conditions may only be required if it is required of all employees with temporary medical conditions per §106.57(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with other Federal and state laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §106.57 obviates a recipient's separate obligation to comply with other civil rights and employment laws, including Title VII as amended by the PDA, Section 504, the ADA, the PWFA, the PUMP Act, the FLSA, and the ACA, and applicable State/local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider overlapping obligations; recent legislation (PWFA, PUMP Act) and pending rulemakings may affect employee accommodations. The Department declined to require certain employee protections now to more fully consider interplay with other employer obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-employment inquiries (§106.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide that recipients may make pre-employment inquiries and may ask applicants to identify their sex under certain conditions; the Department retained and clarified §106.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department asserts these provisions have been part of Title IX regulations since 1975 and are consistent with the Department's grant of regulatory authority to effectuate Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate in employment. The final rule includes minor technical/grammatical clarifications (e.g., adding 'a' before 'pre-employment inquiry' and inserting 'Title IX or' for clarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Title IX coverage (§106.10) — enumerated bases
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule clarifies the scope of Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination and enumerates bases including sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views enumerating these bases as consistent with the broad framing of Title IX and useful for ensuring inclusive, safe learning environments and preventing harassment and discrimination. The Department declined to adopt a definition of 'sex' because it concluded a definition is unnecessary; commenters who urged defining 'sex' in strictly biological terms were considered but the Department maintained a broader approach consistent with statutory interpretation and case law.
